A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain 19 readable pages. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training experiments on synthetic multi-hop reasoning tasks, including accuracy results, curriculum-learning comparisons, probing, and activation-patching analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a model-depth experiment in Appendix C and Table 4.

M1.justification: The GPT-2/RoPE architecture, language-modeling objective, implicit answer generation, and mixed/curriculum learning procedures remain unchanged. The newly tested shallow models are evaluation ablations, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic small and large datasets for 2-, 3-, and 4-hop reasoning. The new depth experiment uses the existing small datasets without introducing different task requirements or data coverage.

E2.justification: The baseline, mixed-learning, and curriculum-learning comparisons remain unchanged, as do the pretrained GPT-2 and larger-model experiments in Appendix B. The shallow-model sweep adds controlled ablations rather than another comparison method.

E3.justification: New Appendix C varies model depth from two to five layers, using fixed training budgets of ×1, ×5, and ×20 for the small 2-, 3-, and 4-hop tasks respectively. Other settings are explicitly retained; existing experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused depth ablation testing whether shallower transformers struggle as reasoning chains lengthen. Existing relation-count, pretraining/model-size, curriculum, and mechanistic analyses are retained, making this a limited supplementary addition.

E5.justification: Both retain three-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting for Sections 4 and 6, with identical entries in v1 Table 8 and v2 Table 9. Appendix B retains single-run reporting; the new depth table introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Table 4 adds 12 depth-dependent accuracy entries. For example, 4-hop-small accuracy at the fixed ×20 budget is 25%, 38%, 83%, and 95% for two through five layers. These are newly reported configurations; retained numerical results and figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 5.1, its bound L ≥ k/(8pdH), the query-independent-attention assumption, and the Appendix A proof and discussion are unchanged. The added depth experiment supplies empirical evidence without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about learnable implicit reasoning, exponential data requirements, depth growth, and partial mitigation through curriculum learning. The depth experiment supports an existing claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 and new Appendix C interpret shallow-model performance as corroborating the theoretical depth prediction. This adds a limited interpretation of the new experiment; existing mechanism explanations, theorem qualifications, and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that code and datasets are available and supplies a repository link in the introduction. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, runtime, and data-generation disclosures are retained; the linked contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior implicit-reasoning, grokking, curriculum-learning, and transformer-theory research are unchanged. The new appendix cites existing sections rather than adding related works.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a short depth-analysis appendix, an accompanying main-text reference, a code-availability sentence, and acknowledgments. Subsequent appendix labels change, while existing prose and narrative organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 4 with depth columns and boldfaces accuracies above 90%. Existing tables are renumbered and several appendix figures and tables move between pages; their displays are retained without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The new depth ablation directly tests a prediction that v1 supported through mechanistic analysis and a conditional theorem, modestly strengthening the empirical case. The code/data pointer also improves reproducibility guidance. These gains remain limited: the experiment is preliminary and confined to existing synthetic tasks, while the original results and theoretical limitations are preserved.
